## Report — PR #116 two-part CodeRabbit fix round, branch `feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed-einstein`

**Consequence first:** both fixes hold up under direct attack, not just re-reading. If shipped as-is, Einstein stops being told about recommendations nobody saw (Fix 1), and a future regression that makes the "Notify me" button explode on click will actually fail CI instead of silently passing (Fix 2). Neither fix touched anything it shouldn't have. **PASS.**

### Per-axis table

| Axis | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Correctness** | PASS | Fresh `npx tsc --noEmit` → clean (exit 0). Fresh `npm run test -- --run` → **93 files / 1371 tests, all green** — matches the claimed count exactly, independently reproduced, not copied from the claim. Cross-checked live PR #116: only two unresolved CodeRabbit review threads exist on the whole PR, both 🟡 Minor, both on exactly these two files/findings — no third finding this round silently skipped. |
| **Pass criteria** | PASS | All 5 items you asked me to check are independently CONFIRMED (detail below), not asserted from the description. |
| **Restraint** | PASS | `git diff --stat` on the working tree = exactly 3 files, +112/-26 lines. No `.bak`/stray files remain (confirmed via `find`). No `console.log`, `.only`/`.skip`, or debugger statements in the diff. Comment updates are proportionate to the one-line logic changes they document. |
| **Conformance** | PASS | No styling/recipe files touched, no new imports added, no tier boundary crossed beyond what was already open on this branch. |
| **Completeness** | PASS | Fix 1 added 3 new tests covering exactly the two bugs it closes (null-survivors-but-over-cap, all-fail-so-no-impression, other-recommenders-unchanged). Fix 2 replaced a no-op assertion with one that provably discriminates pass/fail. No new component was created, so no new story was required. |
| **Design fidelity** | PASS (N/A — nothing rendered changed) | Read the code specifically to confirm this: Fix 1 only slices the impression-tracking effect's local `ids` variable; `<ZimmRecentlyViewedRail cards={cards} .../>` (line 463 of `recommended-products/index.tsx`) still receives the full, unsliced `cards` array, unchanged. Fix 2 is a test-file-only change. There is no visual surface for this round to regress. |

### What I tried to falsify

1. **Fix 2's central, most surprising claim** — that CodeRabbit's own suggested fix (`await user.click(button)`) is *also* a no-op, not just the original `resolves.not.toThrow()`. I did not take this on faith. I wrote a throwaway repro (button whose `onClick` genuinely throws), ran it under this repo's real Vitest/jsdom/React stack, and deleted it afterward. Result: **all 3 tests passed**, including the bare-await one — Vitest logged 3 "Uncaught Exception" entries but never failed the test or rejected the promise. This independently reproduces the claim rather than trusting the docblock.
2. **The shipped `console.error`-spy fix's actual discriminating power.** I mutated the real component (`zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx:270`, changing `onClick={onNotifyMe}` to a version that force-calls it without the optional-chaining safety) and reran the exact shipped test. It **failed** (`TypeError: onNotifyMe is not a function`, Test Files: 1 failed). Restored the file from a byte-identical backup, reran — **27/27 pass**, and `git diff` on that file is empty. This proves the shipped test is a real regression detector, not cosmetic.
3. **The "zero diff on the production component" claim.** Ran `git diff -- .../zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx` directly — empty output, not inferred from `git status`.
4. **The tier-boundary claim**, by going past the rules docs already in my context and grepping the live `CODEOWNERS` file itself: `recommended-products/` is genuinely Tier 2 (`@pwa-squad-b @tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`), and `ui-kits/` (home of `zimmProductCardContent`) is genuinely Tier 3 plain-ownership only, no approver gate — confirming the claim rather than trusting the prose description of it.
5. **`visibleCardCount`'s correctness**, by reading `useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.ts` and `zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx:128-129` side by side: the container and the Rail call the **identical hook**, so the impression cap and the render cap are mathematically the same value at any given commit, not two numbers that merely happen to look similar.

A PASS with no falsification attempt isn't a PASS — the above is what I actually attacked, not what I read and accepted.

### What I could not verify

- Whether the local **CodeRabbit CLI review** (AGENTS.md's mandatory pre-commit step) has been run against this specific working-tree diff — nothing is committed yet (`git status` shows modified-but-unstaged files only), so this is still pending, not something I can check from here.
- Whether **PR review approval** (Tier 2 CODEOWNERS: `tier-2-approvers` + `tier-1-approvers`) has been sought for `recommended-products/` — not part of what I was asked to score, and outside a code-correctness gate's remit.
- I did not re-verify the *original* CodeRabbit findings were real bugs via a fresh independent audit from scratch — I'm relying on your stated separate V&V pass for that, though everything I read about the pre-fix code (the missing `.slice`, the no-op assertion) is independently consistent with the bugs being real.

### Defects

None found. Both fixes are correct, tested, proportionate, and don't cross a tier boundary beyond what was already open on this branch.

### Single biggest residual risk in shipping this step

`visibleCardCount` (container) and `maxVisibleCards` (Rail) agree today only because they call the *same* hook independently in two components — nothing threads one shared value between them. That's safe now, but it's an implicit coupling: if either component's cap computation ever changes on its own (e.g. the Rail someday accepts an override prop, or the container's call gets memoized differently), the impression-count cap and the actual render cap can silently drift apart again — the exact class of bug this fix round just closed.

### What Marcel is missing

The PR's `reviewDecision` is still `CHANGES_REQUESTED` (from CodeRabbit) and both of its unresolved threads are exactly these two findings — but these fixes are sitting uncommitted in the working tree. Nothing on GitHub reflects them yet, and once pushed, AGENTS.md's own rule requires an explicit in-thread reply on both CodeRabbit threads (not just the fix commit) or its learning won't register the resolution.
